title: Unverified Draft: AP Review of Trump's First-Day Promises
description_short: Prior supplied copy says AP reviewed Trump's first-day promises and described legal limits; the linked tracker remains inaccessible.
description_medium: Prior supplied copy says AP reviewed first-day promises Trump made for a return to office, including immigration, birthright citizenship, tariffs, energy and January 6 pardons. It says AP described legal and practical limits. The linked tracker was inaccessible in the supplied research, so these details remain unverified and the March 2026 frozen date is unresolved.
description_long: The packet's earlier draft attributes a January 2025 review to the Associated Press, covering promises Donald Trump said he would address on his first day back in office. According to that supplied draft, the commitments included a large deportation program, closing the border, ending birthright citizenship, imposing tariffs and pardons tied to the January 6 attack. It also says the review distinguished campaign statements from actions a president could take alone and noted possible limits from Congress and the courts. These points are retained only as drafting inputs: the linked AP tracker did not yield readable content in the prior packet, and the live extraction attempt in this review returned HTTP 502. The material does not identify a particular promise row, deadline, implementation status or outcome. The frozen record's March 4, 2026 date does not match the supplied draft's reference to a January 2025 report, and no evidence in the packet resolves that mismatch. This draft therefore makes no finding about promise fulfillment, changing criteria, repeated review cycles, public credibility costs or institutional risk. It is an unverified description of what prior supplied material attributes to AP, pending an accessible source and event date.

title: Bondi Calls for DOJ Working Group to Review Trump and Jan. 6 Cases
description_short: AP reported that after her February 5 swearing-in, Bondi called for a DOJ group to review Trump and Jan. 6 prosecutions.
description_medium: The Associated Press reported that Pam Bondi was sworn in as attorney general on February 5, 2025, and hours later called for a Justice Department “weaponization working group.” AP said the group would scrutinize Jack Smith’s work and review prosecutions stemming from January 6. The report documents a review directive, not a January 20 order to dismiss cases against Trump allies.
description_long: On February 5, 2025, the Associated Press reported that Pam Bondi was sworn in as attorney general and, hours later, called for a Justice Department “weaponization working group.” AP said the group would scrutinize the work of special counsel Jack Smith, who had charged Donald Trump in two criminal cases, and review what Bondi described as “unethical prosecutions” stemming from the January 6, 2021 attack on the Capitol. The supplied original entry instead claimed that Bondi ordered DOJ to drop or suspend a broad set of cases against Trump allies on January 20, including fraud and campaign-finance matters. The date is incompatible with AP’s account of Bondi taking office on February 5, and the AP article describes reviews rather than case dismissals. This correction records the same-day directive AP documents and does not claim that cases were dismissed. It also does not treat the act of reviewing cases as proof of misconduct. The record does not establish which cases, if any, the working group later recommended for action or what outcomes followed.

title: Trump Defended Serena Williams After Her 2009 U.S. Open Semifinal
description_short: Trump’s 2009 blog post defended Serena Williams after her U.S. Open semifinal and criticized the backlash she faced.
description_medium: Reporting on Trump’s 2009 blog says he defended Serena Williams after her U.S. Open semifinal against Kim Clijsters. He objected to the backlash and said Williams had apologized enough. The accessible accounts contradict this entry’s claim that Trump called Williams ugly or a bad person; they do not support its golf reference.
description_long: After Serena Williams’ 2009 U.S. Open semifinal against Kim Clijsters ended in a point penalty following a dispute with a line judge, Trump wrote a blog response defending Williams against public criticism. Sportskeeda quotes him saying, “The backlash against Serena has been relentless and she has been treated badly. She has apologized and I think enough is enough.” The same report says he argued that Williams should be allowed to move on and that the line judge should apologize; a separate account by HITC reproduces those remarks. The reporting contradicts this entry’s original claim that Trump called Williams ugly, a bad person, or bad at golf. This corrected record describes the supported event: Trump’s defense of Williams in response to criticism following the 2009 match. The source accounts do not establish the exact publication date of the original Trump University blog post or the number of people who read it. The frozen August date is also incorrect for the U.S. Open incident, which took place in September 2009.
